title: Endpoint response-quality SLI schema and orchestrated circuit-breaker & regional-shed coordinator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a canonical, production-oriented SLI schema for endpoint response quality that couples latency, functional correctness (promptset-based pass rates), and request-level availability. Design an orchestrator and policy set for circuit-breakers and preemptive regional load-shedding that operate on tenant weight, route priority, and model-variant quality profiles. This ticket produces: (1) SLI definitions and metric names for ingestion, (2) error-budget burn rules and burn-rate thresholds, (3) circuit-breaker state machine and required telemetry, (4) regional ejection thresholds and traffic-steering plan, and (5) a small coordinator service prototype to exercise automatic shedding/fallback on canary traffic.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI document exists that defines request-level success, p50/p90/p99 latency window definitions (first_token and completion), and a response-quality SLI based on curated promptsets with clear aggregation windows
Burn-rate rules are defined: alert (2x expected), automated soft-shed (4x), hard-circuit (10x) with example numeric thresholds applied to a sample endpoint
Coordinator prototype (k8s job) can transition an endpoint through CLOSED -> SOFT_OPEN -> OPEN states and perform: throttle, token-limit, variant-fallback and regional reweighting via routing API
Dashboards and alerts wired to prod metrics: request.latency.ms, request.success.count, response.quality.pass_rate, token.kv_cache.hit, region.capacity.utilization
Runbook snippets included for on-call: how to inspect circuit-breaker state, force reopen, and perform manual regional evacuation

Two nontrivial test cases in staging: (a) synthetic burst that should trigger soft-shed but keep high-priority tenants alive; (b) persistent error spike that triggers regional ejection and circuit-open
decisions: Treat response-quality SLI as a first-class signal (not just latency/availability). Use promptset pass-rate with decayed rolling window (30m) for tradeoff between noise and responsiveness.

Two-tier circuit-breaker: SOFT_OPEN (automated graded shedding, variant-fallback) before OPEN (route-level circuit that rejects low-priority traffic). This reduces blast radius while prioritizing high-tier customers.

Measure success by request-level semantics: a request is 'success' when the model returns a response without runtime error AND passes a lightweight schema/guardrail check; separate path for quality regressions monitored by eval harness.

Regional failover is active-active by default; coordinator can eject a region after 5 minutes of sustained p99/err-rate violation and capacity deficit. Ejection uses weighted traffic reallocation rather than sudden cutover.
Use existing metrics ingestion (Prometheus -> Cortex) names to avoid rework; we will not introduce a new telemetry pipeline in this phase.
Quality-preserving fallback flows are preferred over immediate rejection: try quantized/compatible variant with quality score attached; if variant fails quality SLI, escalate to soft-shed.
Tenant-awareness: use token billing-tier and per-tenant priority to protect critical customers during shedding; background jobs and low-tier tokens are preempted first.
Circuit-breaker state machines live in the coordinator service with eventual consistency; routing layer will observe coordinator decisions via a reconciled API.
We will not attempt model-level automated rollbacks in this ticket; that is covered in release orchestration follow-ups.
tradeoffs: Responsiveness vs stability: shorter aggregation windows make circuit decisions faster but increase false positives. We selected 30m rolling for quality SLI and 5m for latency/availability heuristics to balance sensitivity.

Quality vs availability: fallback to a lower-quality quantized variant improves availability/cost but risks user-visible regressions. To mitigate, we attach 'quality delta' metadata and cap fallback frequency per tenant.

Complexity vs speed: implementing a coordinator service adds operational surface area but centralizes shedding decisions and avoids ad-hoc per-endpoint logic. We accept the operational cost for more predictable policies.

Metric fidelity vs ingestion cost: we reuse existing metrics and add a few high-signal metrics rather than instrumenting every internal queue; this reduces billing/ingest cost at the expense of some granularity.
Ejection vs gradual reweight: hard cutovers minimize cross-region traffic but can increase tail latency for traffic that suddenly lands on other regions; we use graded reweighting to avoid spikes.
Ownership: routing changes require coordination with infra/routing teams; we schedule two integration windows to avoid surprise rollouts.
progress_updates: 2026-01-12: Ticket created after postmortem of INC-2026-01-07 (sustained regional latency). Initial draft of SLI proposals attached.

2026-01-18: Architecture sync with Routing and Console teams. Agreed coordinator will expose a read model and a reconciled routing API. Action: ENG-Routing to add feature flag toggle for staged rollouts (PR #1407).
2026-01-22: Prototype coordinator added to repo (github.com/redwood-inference/coordinator/pull/21). Basic CLOSED -> SOFT_OPEN -> OPEN transitions implemented with metric-driven thresholds mocked.
2026-01-27: Promptset SLI harness design reviewed by Sofia Ramirez (Applied ML). Decided on 250 promptset samples per endpoint to compute pass_rate with 30m decay.

2026-01-30: Load test in staging: synthetic 5x burst triggered soft-shed as expected; high-priority tenants maintained with token-priority. Observed token.kv_cache.hit drop correlating with latency increase—added cache-miss guard to acceptance criteria.
2026-02-05: Policy doc reviewed by Product (Ethan Zhou) and Security (Leah Morgan). Security asked for audit events on circuit transitions; added event emission requirement.
review_comments: Product (Ethan Zhou): Make sure acceptance criteria include observable evidence that quality SLI doesn't regress for top 10 customers during soft-shed testing.
Design (Sofia Ramirez): Promptset selection should include adversarial prompts and multi-turn context to catch regressions that surface only on longer histories.
Routing (Diego Alvarez): Coordinator API must support idempotent reconcile calls and a versioned decision payload to avoid thrash across regions.
Security (Leah Morgan): Add immutable audit log events and integrate with central KMS for signing coordinator actions. No sensitive data should be emitted in events.
Infra (Nina Chen): During regional ejection we need rate-limited, batched reweights to avoid transient overload on remaining regions. Add rate cap in coordinator config.
